title: Goal Review Assessment Practice
opening: Goals that make sense separately can compete for the same time, attention or support. Review them together before deciding that another goal is what you need.

labels.comparison: Can two priorities use the same hour?
labels.comparisonIntro: Suppose someone values two projects, but both require the same protected hour after work. Calling both a priority does not create another hour. Compare the goals with the life they serve and the resources they actually receive.
labels.adherenceText: Each project may serve something important. The review starts by naming what each contributes, rather than treating the conflict as proof that one goal is worthless.
labels.valueText: If both projects require the same hour, the combined plan cannot give each the full hour. Look at actual participation, other commitments and available support. A lack of daily action might reflect a poor arrangement or a missing resource rather than a lack of value.
labels.outcomeText: The person could sequence the projects, reduce one project’s scope or seek suitable support. Which choice helps depends on what each goal needs and what else the change affects. Adding another goal leaves this conflict unresolved.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmTitle: Review the set of goals, not just each goal alone
labels.rhythmText: List what you currently pursue and compare it with the life and values those goals should serve. Inspect the action and resources each receives, then look for conflicts and important omissions. Choose what needs examination before adding more. A valued experience does not always need to become a target, and one clear urgent action may need no full inventory.
labels.practiceIntro: Keep the parts of the review that help you see what needs attention. You can start with a single pair of competing goals and return with more information.

labels.sourceQuote:
Goal Review Assessment Practice
List the goals you currently pursue. Compare each with the life and values it is
meant to serve, the daily action it receives and the other commitments it affects.
Identify an important area without a corresponding goal, or two goals whose
demands conflict. Choose what needs examination before adding another goal.

fields.label: The life and values these goals should serve
The action, time and support they actually receive
A conflict among their demands or effects
An important omission, if you notice one

example.qualities: Prepare a useful workshop and finish a research article.
example.contribution: Help people investigate questions well and understand the topic more deeply.
example.avoid: Both projects currently rely on the same hour after work.
example.present: The workshop rehearsal and article analysis are each planned for the whole hour.
example.connection: I have left no recovery time around these commitments.
example.change: Compare the real deadlines, then consider sequencing or reducing scope before adding another project.
